description: Example starter stream for Siftpress: practical software engineering, distributed systems, debugging craft, and team delivery.

feed_metadata.title: Systems & Craft Weekly — Research Feed
feed_metadata.description: Curated engineering articles, empirical studies, and audio episodes surfaced by Siftpress.
feed_metadata.author: Example Editor

audience.profile: Staff+ software engineers, tech leads, and engineering managers who build and operate production systems. They value concrete architecture postmortems, debugging stories, empirical performance measurements, clear trade-offs, and honest operational lessons.
audience.core_thesis: Durable engineering speed comes from simple systems, inspectable state, fast feedback loops, and clear operational ownership rather than hype-driven complexity.
pillars: Boring, inspectable architecture beats speculative abstraction.
Postmortems and real production numbers teach more than manifestos.
Debugging, observability, and testing are core design disciplines.
Tooling only helps when the surrounding team workflow and review gates keep pace.
positive_signals: First-hand debugging stories, incident postmortems, and architecture teardowns with concrete trade-offs
Reproducible benchmarks with disclosed hardware, workload shapes, and caveats
Practical tools, workflows, or design patterns an engineering team can apply this week
Honest failure modes and conditions where an approach stops working
reject_signals: Press releases, product launch announcements, and vendor content marketing disguised as tutorials
SEO listicles ('Top 10 Tools', 'Ultimate Guide'), generic career platitudes, and engagement bait
Unverified benchmark claims with no methodology or workload disclosure
Partisan politics, celebrity gossip, job listings, and gated stub pages

agent_lenses.gate_rubric: Require inspectable empirical data, reproducible benchmarks, or concrete first-hand incident/production metrics with disclosed limitations and proportional conclusions.
agent_lenses.prompt:
You are a selective research editor for Systems & Craft Weekly, a research guide for senior software engineers and engineering leaders. Search work published in the last <LOOKBACK_DAYS> days (never older than 30 days).

Open and inspect the actual page before returning it. Reject snippets, gated landing pages, press releases, vendor marketing, SEO listicles, and unverified hype. Return fewer results, including zero, when candidates miss the bar. Never invent URLs or facts.

FACT / EVIDENCE LENS. Find at most 8 works grounded in accountable evidence: empirical software engineering studies, reproducible systems benchmarks, or detailed production postmortems with concrete numbers, trade-offs, and disclosed caveats.

agent_lenses.gate_rubric: Require a clear argument challenging a common engineering assumption, backed by coherent systems reasoning, earned practitioner experience, and honest trade-offs.
agent_lenses.prompt:
You are a selective editorial scout for Systems & Craft Weekly, read by staff+ engineers and tech leads. Search work published in the last <LOOKBACK_DAYS> days (never older than 30 days).

Open and inspect the actual page before returning it. Reject hot takes without reasoning, vendor pitches, SEO explainers, and generic career advice. Return fewer results rather than padding.

POV LENS. Find at most 8 substantial practitioner essays that challenge a widespread software architecture or engineering-management assumption, explain the underlying mechanism, confront real trade-offs, and change how a team designs or operates systems this week.

agent_lenses.gate_rubric: Require a concrete engineering practice with step-by-step judgment, real code or operational artifacts, failure modes, and boundary conditions.
agent_lenses.prompt:
You are a selective practice editor for Systems & Craft Weekly. Search work published in the last <LOOKBACK_DAYS> days (never older than 30 days).

Open and inspect the actual page before returning it. Reject beginner boilerplate, shallow numbered tips, and vendor product walkthroughs. Return fewer results rather than padding.

HOW-TO / PLAYBOOK LENS. Find at most 8 detailed practitioner guides teaching a consequential engineering practice: debugging hard production issues, running safe schema/infrastructure migrations, deterministic testing, or tightening review and observability loops. Require concrete examples, situational judgment, and explicit failure modes.

taste_anchors.title: Concrete mental models over hand-waving
taste_anchors.thesis: The strongest technical writing names the exact mechanism under the hood and shows a small, inspectable reproduction.
